# Create E5 Swarm gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the E5 Swarm enemy — the fast-moving, unpredictable cluster attacker from GDD §4.1. The scene should show its small, diamond-shaped neon entities moving in tight, fast clusters with sudden direction changes. This is the highest-threat regular enemy by positional threat in dense formations.

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing enemy behaviour — wants to see the Swarm's fast, chaotic cluster movement in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of swarm/clustering movement patterns.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see Swarm enemies move in tight, fast-moving clusters that change direction suddenly so I can verify the cluster movement logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to destroy a random Swarm enemy and see its explosion animation so I can verify destruction logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to toggle the Swarm's shooting behaviour on/off so I can test both cluster-only and shooting modes independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts`) renders Swarm enemies in tight, fast-moving clusters.
- [ ] **AC2 — Swarm visual style:** Swarms render as small, diamond-shaped neon entities (blue `#0066ff` per GDD §4.1) in groups, consistent with the player ship aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Cluster movement:** Enemies move in tight, fast-moving clusters that change direction suddenly. Clusters stay together but can split and rejoin.
- [ ] **AC4 — Explode button:** A button on-screen destroys a random Swarm enemy with an explosion animation when clicked.
- [ ] **AC5 — Toggle shoot button:** A button toggles whether Swarms fire coordinated burst shots (simulating Level 4 behaviour). When off, Swarms only cluster. When on, they fire coordinated bursts.
- [ ] **AC6 — Enemy pass-through verified:** Swarms pass freely through each other without collision (per GDD §2.6).
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** Swarms are 1 HP, destroyed by a single bullet. No health bar needed.
- **Cluster dynamics:** Swarms should feel fast and unpredictable. Clusters of 3–5 enemies move together, can split and rejoin.
- **Firing:** When shoot mode is toggled on, Swarms fire coordinated bursts (multiple enemies firing simultaneously in the same direction).
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, fast movement whoosh, and destruction (sharp, quick sound).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` — The Swarm gym scene.
- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — Swarm enemy entity (cluster movement + coordinated firing logic).
- `src/assets/` — Swarm sprite (blue diamond shape).
- `src/audio/` — Swarm-related sound effects (spawn, movement, destruction).

## Related work

- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — related; implements V-formation pattern.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; will refactor code across enemy gym scenes.
- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — related; will link to this scene from the gym index.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec, §4.1 E5 Swarm definition.

## Best practices (mandatory — see docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

This scene MUST be built on the shared core gym formation-scene library and follow the conventions documented in **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`** (see §3 "Best practice: adding a new enemy gym scene" and §5 "Extending the core library"). In particular:

- Extend `GymFormationScene` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) wherever the scene is a formation-driven gym scene; supply only entity-specific configuration (`EnemyFormationConfig`), constants, and thin test accessors — DO NOT copy the ~200-line formation/UI/bullet boilerplate from the pre-refactor `GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`.
- Movement that exceeds `applyFormationPosition()`'s flat-translation contract (e.g. E4 orbital paths, E5 clusters, Boss phases) belongs in the **entity** or as a new seam in the core library per §5 — never by duplicating scene boilerplate.
- Reuse the shared formation-offset builders in `src/utils/formations.ts` for any grid/formation geometry; add new pure builders there with unit tests.
- Follow the new-scene checklist: `add.existing()` for display-list membership, `lineStyle()` after `clear()` in entity drawing, exported tuning constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests (spawn count, geometry, drift, EXPLODE, SHOOT toggle, `← INDEX`).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1/§3 if this scene introduces a new convention.

- [ ] **AC9 — Core library reuse:** The scene extends the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (or an approved core-library seam per §5 of `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) and contains no duplicated formation/UI/bullet boilerplate.
- [ ] **AC10 — Guide compliance:** The implementation follows the new-scene checklist in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§3): `add.existing()`, `lineStyle()` after `clear()`, exported constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests.
